title: docs(fields): teach the two-step cell-renderer resolve, name the exported registrar
body:
Fixes #8294
Fixes #8292

Two claims on `packages/fields/README.md`, one file, one fence and one line. Landed together on the triage seat's routing: same file, same batch-36 origin, two PRs on this page would only collide.

Implemented by the os-dev seat, session `session_01611D6ZaRaMmwTNQmSbk8MH`.

## ⚠️ Correction — this body undercounted the population, and said so in a load-bearing place

An earlier revision of this body claimed **five** shipped `getCellRenderer(` call sites, and stated that **"Every shipped consumer is already correct, so nothing in the product is currently wrong."** Both were false. The second one was not a stray sentence: it was the severity argument. The same false universal had also reached the published page, as the fence comment's closing sentence — *"Every shipped view calls this pair."* That sentence is deleted in this round.

Re-measured on the merge result (`9ec59f498`) — non-test `getCellRenderer(` call-site lines outside `packages/fields`:

| | count |
|---|---|
| call-site **lines** | **15** |
| files | **10** |
| published packages | **6** |
| — of those lines, resolve the key first | **10** |
| — pass the field's declared `type` **raw** | **4** |
| — a string literal that is not a field type at all | **1** |

The four raw sites are all in `packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx`, at lines 2675, 2832, 2953 and 4400. `TextCellRenderer` never reads `field.format`, so a `Field.text({ format: 'phone' })` column renders as bare text in the flagship grid today, with nothing thrown and nothing logged. **That is a live product defect, not a teaching gap.** It is out of scope for this docs-only PR and is carried by objectui#8920. The one literal is `getCellRenderer('select')` at `ObjectGrid.tsx:2607`, the badge-prefix widget — no field is involved, so it is neither correct nor incorrect on this axis.

### Instrument, and the two traps it had to survive

Enumeration and reading come from the **same ref** (`git grep -n 'getCellRenderer(' HEAD`), then non-test / non-`packages/fields` / non-markdown lines are classified by tracing each argument's **binding to its initializer** — never by the identifier's spelling. Both controls fired:

- **Per-file grep reports 10 of 10 green, and is wrong.** Every one of the 10 files imports and uses `resolveCellRendererType` somewhere (ObjectGrid uses it 3 times, at `:30`, `:2454`, `:2469`). The property is per **call site**, not per file.
- **A spelling scan reports 9 of 15 resolving, and is wrong.** `ObjectGrid.tsx:2675` and `:2832` each bind a variable literally named `resolvedType`, whose initializer is `fieldDef?.type || inferColumnType(...)` — the **declared** type, which never passed through the resolver. A probe matching `getCellRenderer(resolvedSomething)` slides straight past both.

Positive control on the enumeration side: the same pattern and ref hit the definition, `export function getCellRenderer` at `packages/fields/src/index.tsx:2697`.

## What changed

**#8294 — the fence's argument.** The "Using Standard Fields" block resolved the renderer straight off the field's declared type. `field.type` is not always the renderer's key: for a textual base type carrying a `format` hint, `resolveCellRendererType` maps to the richer renderer. The fence now teaches the two steps, with a comment saying why.

The comment's closing claim is now true **by construction rather than by census**: with no format hint the resolver returns the declared type unchanged (`return fieldOrType.type || 'text'`, the final line of `resolveCellRendererType`), so resolving first is never worse than not. That is read off the resolver itself and cannot rot when call sites move — which is precisely how the deleted sentence went false.

The prose sentence one line above the fence is true as written and is **untouched** — the defect was the argument, not the sentence.

**#8292 — a symbol nothing exports.** The Features list named `FieldRegistry`. Measured: zero occurrences in the tree apart from that line, and no such declaration in the built `.d.ts`. The role it described is borne by `registerFieldRenderer`, which **is** exported and which the fence one screen below already calls. The line now names it. The backing `const fieldRegistry` Map stays module-private, so naming *it* was never an option; this replaces a phantom reference with a real one rather than with another guess.

## Why the green gates are not the evidence

`getCellRenderer(field.type)` **type-checks** — `field.type` is a string, the parameter is a string — so `check:doc-snippets` read the old block green, 0 diagnostics. A green that cannot go red on this defect is not evidence the example was right.

**And no gate reads the deleted sentence either.** The doc gate compiles the fence's *code*; the false universal lived in a *comment*, and nothing in the tree pins this page's prose (a whole-tree `git grep` for `fields/README` returns zero hits). A census was the only instrument that could ever have caught it — which is why this body now states its instrument rather than pointing at a check mark.

The oracle for the fix itself is the shipped behaviour. Measured against the built `dist` (the same entry a consumer imports), rendering a `Field.text({ format: 'phone' })` column both ways:

| | resolved key | `tel:` anchor | threw |
|---|---|---|---|
| README as written | `text` | **no** | no — silent |
| README as fixed | `phone` | **yes** | no — silent |

The old fence produced `span class="block max-w-full truncate"` around the bare number; the new one produces `a href="tel:+1-415-555-0134"`. Neither leg throws, which is the defect's whole shape: a copied cell drops the format hint and nothing anywhere reports it.

## Severity

`priority:p3` stands **for this PR**, whose blast radius is bounded to whoever copies this fence. It no longer rests on the retracted universal. The product defect that universal concealed is real and is graded on its own card, objectui#8920 — the flagship grid dropping format hints on four paths.

## Verification

**Base merged in, not rebased.** `origin/main` (`829a7067c`) was merged into the branch as a merge commit (`05d3d0e6b`); no rebase, no force-push. Every number below was then measured on that merge result at head `9ec59f498`. Diff versus `origin/main`: 2 files, +23 / −3 — `packages/fields/README.md` and the changeset, nothing under `packages/fields/src`.

| Check | Verdict |
|---|---|
| build closure (`--build-filter`, `--concurrency=2`) | exit 0 — 35/35 turbo tasks successful |
| `check:doc-snippets` | exit 0 — 796 covered blocks, 638 compiled, 0 failed |
| ↳ same, under an injected arity error in **this** fence | exit 1 — `packages/fields/README.md:52:68 TS2554: Expected 1 arguments, but got 2`, 638 judged / 1 failed |
| ↳ restore leg | on-disk blob byte-equal to the HEAD blob (`d5e5b022c`), `git diff HEAD` empty, gate back to exit 0 |
| `check:readme-exports` | exit 0 — 539 self-imports judged, 0 fabricated |
| `check:doc-examples` | exit 0 — 125 blocks, 90/90 ledger rows intact |
| `check:doc-fences` / `check:doc-links` / `check:control-bytes` / `check:unreferenced-sources` | exit 0 |
| `census:cross-file-line-citations` | exit 0 — no citation targets this file |
| `check:changeset-presence` | exit 0 — none owed; the empty-frontmatter declaration stands |

⚠️ **One NOT MEASURED, then measured.** The first `check:doc-examples` run exited **2** — PREREQUISITE NOT MET, `dist` absent — which is neither green nor red. It was re-run after the build closure and is the exit 0 in the table.

The arity-injection control is re-pinned to this head, not carried over from the previous round: the mutation was proved on disk in both directions (clean form 1 → 0, mutated form 0 → 1) before the gate was run, and the restore was verified by blob hash rather than by an exit code.

## Changeset

`.changeset/8294-fields-readme-cell-renderer-two-step.md`, empty frontmatter — an explicit "no release". `scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` independently judged none owed: "0 of them published source of a package the release covers, 0 of them a manifest whose published contract moved". Declaring it once beats staying silent, since `README.md` is in this package's `files[]` and therefore does ship in the tarball.

## 验收备注

Noted while measuring, **not** filed and not touched here:

- objectui#8920 is cited in the commit message and in this body, but deliberately **not** in the README. That page is the published consumer document for `@object-ui/fields`; an open defect card about a sibling package's internals does not belong on it, and would rot the moment the card lands.
- The section heading "Field Registry" and its sentence at line 19 describe the mechanism in plain prose, not as a backticked symbol, so they are not phantom references and stay as they are.
- `check:readme-exports` reports 1 unbuilt package and 3 declaring no types; `census:cross-file-line-citations` reports pre-existing drifted and out-of-range citations in `scripts/check-vi-mock-specifiers.mjs`, `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs` and `scripts/vite-dts-fail-on-type-errors.ts`. All pre-existing on `main`, all outside this diff, both gates exit 0.
